title: The dynamics of stable matchings and half-matchings for the stable marriage and roommates problems
summary_en: In stable matching problems — the algorithm behind kidney-exchange and school-choice systems — the standard theory assumes full matchings exist. Biró, Cechlárová and Fleiner study what happens when only a 'half-matching' (some agents partially matched) is feasible and ask how the dynamics of partner-swapping evolve toward a stable outcome. The paper extends the classical Gale–Shapley framework to settings where rejection cascades are common and characterises convergence of the resulting dynamic process.
data_used: Theoretical paper. No primary dataset; results are derived analytically for the stable-marriage and stable-roommates problems.
policy_relevance: Underpins the design of matching mechanisms used in real-world Hungarian and EU allocation problems — kidney-exchange networks (where Hungary participates in EU programmes), school-place allocation, residency matching for medical graduates. The dynamic-stability results inform robustness of these mechanisms when not all agents can be matched in equilibrium.
